# Data classes and retention

Every classified column on the platform, and what happens to it, per [ADR-0301](../adr/0301-data-lifecycle-privacy.md).

A new service is reviewed against this checklist. Without it, a service can omit its obligations and nobody sees it. The gap then shows on the first erasure request that needs it, at best a month before the deadline.

**It is a view, not a source.** The classes come from the `pii:<class>` tags in the migrations. The tag lives in the DDL and moves with the schema. The periods and disposals come from `tools/codegen/retention.yaml`. A column tag cannot hold how long to keep a class, or whether to delete or anonymise it. An edit to this file changes nothing: add the tag, or change the policy.

## Policy per class

| Class | Retention | At the end | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `contact` | life of the account, then 30 days | delete | Email, phone, postal address. It identifies a person directly, so an erasure request removes it and does not anonymise it. |
| `device` | 90 days | delete | IP address, user agent, device identifier. Raw IP addresses are never stored, per ADR-0700. This class covers what is left after reduction. |
| `financial` | 7 years | anonymise | Payment instrument details. The period is a bookkeeping obligation, not a product decision. It overrides an erasure request for the row's financial fields. |
| `free_text` | life of the account, then 30 days | delete | A field that a user types into, which can hold anything. It gets the strictest likely class, because its contents cannot be predicted. |
| `government_id` | only while a legal obligation requires it | delete | National identifier, passport, tax number. The shortest period of any class, because the risk is to hold one with no current obligation. |
| `identifier` | life of the account, then 30 days | anonymise | A pseudonymous subject or account identifier. It is anonymised, not deleted, because rows keyed by it, such as orders and charges, have their own retention obligation. That obligation outlives the account. |
| `location` | 90 days | delete | Coordinates and precise geolocation. |
| `name` | life of the account, then 30 days | delete | A person's name. |
| `none` | not applicable | not applicable | Checked, and holds no personal data. The tag shows that someone decided, so it differs from a column nobody checked. |
| `special_category` | only while a legal obligation requires it | delete | GDPR Art. 9 data, such as health and biometrics. The platform stores none. The class exists so that adding one is a deliberate act against a stated rule. |

## What this does not cover

[ADR-0500](../adr/0500-observability.md) owns telemetry retention, and [ADR-0200](../adr/0200-cluster-topology.md) owns backup retention. This registry owns application data, which is the part that an erasure request reaches.

A column tagged `pii:none` appears here too, on purpose. The tag shows that someone checked the column and found no personal data. Without the tag, nobody can tell that from a column nobody checked.
